answer.rationale: With the line at 94% of committed volume and zero buffer, any supplier transition (switch_primary_vendor) carries acute delivery-interruption risk that outweighs potential cost savings, especially under a 14-day contract deadline that leaves no room for onboarding hiccups. memory_c1 shows incumbent renewals preserve delivery continuity, while memory_c4 shows renegotiation at renewal previously recovered real margin and improved payment terms without touching integration or delivery schedules — directly addressing the 18% cost mandate without introducing new supply-chain risk. I want to verify memory_c4's original record before committing, since it's the single memory carrying the most weight for this decision and its consolidated summary ('recovered real margin') is vague enough that I want to confirm the actual negotiated terms and conditions rather than assume magnitude. Switching vendors (memory_c2) or adding a second source (memory_c3) are plausible future moves but are better suited to the next review cycle once there's more buffer or lead time to de-risk a transition. Deferring (memory_c5) isn't viable here since this is explicitly a critical, expiring, non-auto-renewing contract, unlike the non-critical case in that memory. I'm flagging downstream risk because aggressive cost-cutting pressure could tempt overreach into vendor switching territory that the current capacity buffer can't safely absorb, and I'm preserving uncertainty since a single archived memory shouldn't be treated as guaranteed replicable savings without checking the source.
